11.speaker: Monica
11.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: I was sitting in my office. I looked at the clock.

19.speaker: Ciara Walda
19.text: "It's a pity your wife won't be joining us."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: 2:26 PM. It was almost time for my appointment with Ciara on women's rights.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: There was a knock at the door. Ciara entered the room with folders in her hand. The door did not close behind her.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: Monica entered the room and stood next to Ciara.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: Monica entered the room and stood next to Ciara. I was confused. This was the opposite of what we had agreed after the Benfi Festival.

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Right before she made her way out, her eyes met with Monica's and the two women exchanged nods. The door closed, leaving Monica and me alone in the office.

32.speaker: Player
32.text: "How dare you show up here after what we agreed!"

34.speaker: Monica
34.text: “I know, but...I just thought you would say no again.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “You were damn right. I would say no, and I am saying no."

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “Don't we have any trust in each other anymore?”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “So you went behind my back to join this meeting?”

38.speaker: Monica
38.text: “You know how much I want to help women in Sordland. I had an opportunity and I couldn't let it pass.”

39.speaker: Monica
39.text: “You also know how stubborn I am. Once I set my mind on something, I won't budge.”

40.speaker: Monica
40.text: “You have my trust always. But this is a greater cause than just the two of us. I wouldn't have done this if I didn't believe that."

41.speaker: Monica
41.text: “We finally have the chance to change things for Sordish women. There's no way I was going to let that opportunity pass."

42.speaker: Monica
42.text: “Anton, please try to understand. I wouldn't do this if I didn't think this was necessary.”

43.speaker: Monica
43.text: “We're at a place where we can finally change the status of Sordish women. I couldn't let this opportunity pass.”

44.speaker: Monica
44.text: “So when Ciara asked me to join her today, I had to accept."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “Ciara needs to learn that she can't interfere with my family.”

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “This doesn't change the fact that you didn't trust me.”

47.speaker: Player
47.text: “To be honest, I would've done the same if that is what it took to get my word across.”

48.speaker: Monica
48.text: “I know. And I'm sorry. Will you...will you forgive me?”

49.speaker: Monica
49.text: “Don't blame her. She just did what was necessary for the future of Sordish women.”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “If you promise never to surprise me like this again."

56.speaker: Monica
56.text: “Thank you, Anton. I will tell you everything from now on.”

59.speaker: Player
59.text: “My answer is still no. You will not go into politics.”

60.speaker: Monica
60.text: “But why? This is about Sordish women. This is bigger than just politics.”

61.speaker: Player
61.text: “It's simply too dangerous. I don't want you to get hurt.”

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “Don't be naive. Everything comes down to politics in the end.”

63.speaker: Monica
63.text: “I understand the danger, but someone has to do it.”

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: She hugged me and kissed me on the cheek.

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “No canoodling at work, Mrs. First Lady.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “All right. Can you call Ciara back?”

68.speaker: Monica
68.text: “I'll fetch Ciara so we can get started."

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: Monica left the office and returned with Ciara. Both women were smiling.

73.speaker: Monica
73.text: “I know I don't understand politics the way you and Ciara do. But my role would be that of a spokeswoman. That's all.”

74.speaker: Monica
74.text: “You know how much I want to help women in Sordland. I had an opportunity, and I couldn't let it pass."

75.speaker: Monica
75.text: “Ciara approached me about it. I had to accept."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Why didn't you tell her I forbade it?"

78.speaker: Monica
78.text: “Do you think she'd take that for an answer?"

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “Look, I'm sorry for yelling. But we talked about this before and I clearly said it would be a bad idea."

80.speaker: Monica
80.text: “I know it was a surprise to you. I'm sorry. I will tell you everything from now on.”

82.speaker: Monica
82.text: “Why should a wife need her husband's permission to do something?”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “What are you going to do? Leave me? You wouldn't dare."

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: She walked to the door and wrenched it open. She walked away and closed the door with a loud slam.

87.speaker: Monica
87.text: “There are things at play here that are greater than just us.”

88.speaker: Monica
88.text: “Look. I will be blunt. If you want to remain happily married, you will let me do this. I need this. Sordish women need this.”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “Can't you let Ciara do that? She is more experienced.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “You don't know how hard it is to be in that position. I'm trying to protect you.”

92.speaker: Monica
92.text: “I understand that. At least I think I do. But I really need to do this. For my own dignity as a Sordish woman and to root out the evil inside people like Curtan Leste.”

93.speaker: Monica
93.text: “Ciara has the experience, but people think she's a radical, and un-feminine at that. She's not popular enough with the public to get this message across. I am.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “I'm sorry, but I can't let you do that. Please understand.”

95.speaker: Monica
95.text: “This is my line in the sand, Anton. Now that I'm here, I won't back down."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: “Very well. If it's that important to you, stay."

97.speaker: Monica
97.text: “Then I hope you will understand this.”

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: Before I could say anything, she got up and left my office.

102.speaker: Monica
102.text: “I'll go fetch Ciara so we can get started.”

103.speaker: Narrator
103.text: Monica briefly left the office and returned with Ciara. The two women were smiling.

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: Monica looked down at the floor, then back up at me.

109.speaker: Player
109.text: “Then believe me when I say: don't get involved in politics."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: I stood there for a few minutes as I contemplated what had just happened. Eventually, Ciara knocked and entered my office again.

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: I stood in silence for a few minutes, contemplating what had just happened, Eventually, Ciara knocked and entered my office again.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: Monica left the office. A short time later, Ciara knocked on the door.

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “We are getting close to the elections. I can't handle any possible bad press.”

117.speaker: Monica
117.text: “I know Benfi may have crossed a line, but this is different.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “This is my final answer. You will not do it.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “All right. If you are willing to take the risk, I will let you do it.”

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: She made her way to the door.

127.speaker: Monica
127.text: “I just wanted to thank you for agreeing to this meeting."

129.speaker: Monica
129.text: “I've been dreaming about this ever since I volunteered with the Sordish League of Women. I can't believe the moment's finally here."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “I think both of you together could finally bring change to Sordland.”

133.speaker: Monica
133.text: "Not just me, Anton. All of us."

134.speaker: Player
134.text: “I hope you thought this through. Real change requires carefully considered plans.”

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: After a couple of knocks at the door, Ciara entered the room with folders in her hand.

140.speaker: Ciara Walda
140.text: “Not a particularly auspicious start to this meeting. But let's begin."

153.speaker: Ciara Walda
153.text: “And this isn't only a moral issue. I have seen enough revolutions in this world to understand the main driver of any change.”

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: Ciara sat down on a chair and laid down the folder she was holding.

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: She flipped a folder open and started pulling out documents.

156.speaker: Ciara Walda
156.text: “In United Contana, law dictates that women earn the same wages as men in their respective fields. My research shows that this led to a 15.5% increase in productivity. You could say this had a direct influence on their superpower status.”

157.speaker: Ciara Walda
157.text: "Arcasia passed laws ensuring maternity leave rights, child day care centers and tax deductions for working families. In turn, they experienced a 12.6% productivity boost and a flourishing economy."

158.speaker: Ciara Walda
158.text: “Both countries also have significantly lower infant mortality rates, a statistic I believe is directly linked to the improved status of women.”

159.speaker: Ciara Walda
159.text: “Our administration has successfully managed to pull Sordland back from the brink of economic ruin."

163.speaker: Ciara Walda
163.text: “Our administration has thus far failed to pull Sordland out of its economic recession."

164.speaker: Ciara Walda
164.text: “So I am asking: Why stop there? Why not improve our economy and modernize our society at the same time?"

165.speaker: Ciara Walda
165.text: “So I am asking: Why not try passing similar laws? At worst, even if they fail to improve the economy, it'll still be a significant step forward for our society."

166.speaker: Narrator
166.text: She leaned back in her chair.

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: She leaned back in her chair.

169.speaker: Player
169.text: “It feels too much like you're comparing Sordland to other nations. We must choose our own path.”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “You've made a good case for all of these changes.”

171.speaker: Ciara Walda
171.text: “I want to establish a commission for women's rights in Sordland with me as its head. Our goal shall be passing and implementing a set of laws to solve the problems we just discussed."

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: Ciara handed me one of the documents. It had a list of bullet points on it.

173.speaker: Monica
173.text: “Or even as their counterparts in Arcasia and United Contana. We've been lagging behind on this for decades, Anton."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: “I'm not sure I can risk passing laws like these so close to the election.”

177.speaker: Ciara Walda
177.text: “These laws would result in greater productivity, a better economy *and* happier women -- to be frank, Mr. President, you'd have to be a fool not to pass them."

178.speaker: Ciara Walda
178.text: “If we can pull this off before the elections, the Rayne administration will make history.”

179.speaker: Ciara Walda
179.text: “I agree completely. We must aim to be better than them. Better than all the superpowers.”

180.speaker: Ciara Walda
180.text: “None of them have yet managed to achieve true parity among the sexes. If we can do that, we'll make history.”

185.speaker: Ciara Walda
185.text: “Or even as their counterparts in Arcasia and United Contana. We've been lagging behind on this for decades."

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Monica handed me one of the documents. It had a list of bullet points on it.

193.speaker: Monica
193.text: “As the commission's spokeswoman, my responsibility will be to make speeches and organize fundraisers. I will be the face of this movement while Ciara handles the groundwork."

194.speaker: Monica
194.text: “If I can show that the First Lady is behind this movement, many women will feel encouraged.”

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: Ciara gestured down at her outfit.

196.speaker: Ciara Walda
196.text: “The organization's name will be 'Commission on the Status of Women'.”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “Why bother with a commission? I can pass the laws you want here and now."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “It's going to be damn hard getting your laws past the Assembly."

199.speaker: Ciara Walda
199.text: “You'll still need to make sure they're effectively implemented.”

200.speaker: Ciara Walda
200.text: “Mr. President, I know we've had friction in the past -- whether over the failed education reform, or the teaching of creationism."
200.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

201.speaker: Ciara Walda
201.text: “This is a completely separate topic and it should be handled as such.”

202.speaker: Ciara Walda
202.text: “Mr. President, I know we've had friction in the past. But this has nothing to do with the failed education reform."
202.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

203.speaker: Ciara Walda
203.text: “Mr. President, I know we've had friction in the past. But this has nothing to do with your decisions on creationism."
203.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

207.speaker: Ciara Walda
207.text: “One more thing to consider before making your decision. This could help silence any of the public's lingering questions regarding your former vice president and the Livia Suno affair."
207.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

208.speaker: Ciara Walda
208.text: “One more thing to consider before making your decision. This could help silence any of the public's lingering questions regarding your vice president and the Livia Suno affair."
208.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_DenyEverything"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

209.speaker: Ciara Walda
209.text: “You have the chance to be a hero. Think about your daughter and her future.”
209.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_DenyEverything"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false)

210.speaker: Ciara Walda
210.text: “I hope you will make the right decision.”

214.speaker: Monica
214.text: “And that man would want a better future for his daughter and her daughters. No matter what else he's said or done."

215.speaker: Monica
215.text: “I hope you'll make the right decision. We both do."

216.speaker: Narrator
216.text: They rose from their seats expectantly.

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: Ciara rose from her seat expectantly.

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: I took a few minutes to think.

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “I'm on your side. But I want to go through the Assembly. Can't risk a backlash this close to the election.”

223.speaker: Player
223.text: “I hereby declare your laws passed and your commission established. Good luck." [Sign Decree. -2 Government Budget]

224.speaker: Player
224.text: “I will approve the creation of the commission and support your bill in the Assembly.”

225.speaker: Ciara Walda
225.text: “Great. Amazing. You won't regret this, Mr. President."

226.speaker: Ciara Walda
226.text: “Then all is lost for the future of women in Sordland.”

227.speaker: Ciara Walda
227.text: “Your female constituents will remember you as a failure.”

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: She looked at Monica. She was silent for a moment.

233.speaker: Monica
233.text: “How do I explain this to Deana, once she's old enough to understand? How do I tell her about all the opportunities she could have had, that her own father denied her?”

234.speaker: Narrator
234.text: Without waiting for my answer, she pushed her chair aside and stormed out. Ciara followed suit, and I could hear the two of them talking angrily as the door closed behind them.

235.speaker: Narrator
235.text: Ciara furiously gathered up her documents.

236.speaker: Narrator
236.text: I sagged back in my chair and exhaled. It was a clear day outside, but the perfect view over Holsord provided little comfort.

247.speaker: Player
247.text: “I know. That's why I already signed the decree to give women an equal education."

248.speaker: Monica
248.text: “Yes, and that was a major step forward. But there's so much more work that must be done."

252.speaker: Monica
252.text: “See, that's why this meeting is so necessary!"

253.speaker: Player
253.text: “Someone has to stay home and look after Deana.”

254.speaker: Monica
254.text: “I'm doing this *for* Deana. And for so many other girls like her.”

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "This isn't about joining a knitting circle or having a friend for tea. It's about my career!"

256.speaker: Player
256.text: "I promise I take women's rights seriously. Just let Ciara handle this."

257.speaker: Player
257.text: "Because you'll make me look foolish otherwise -- like you did at the Benfi Festival."

261.speaker: Monica
261.text: "Your career. For which you have consistently sidelined me and your children."

262.speaker: Monica
262.text: "I had dreams of a career too, back in university. But I gave those up for you."

263.speaker: Monica
263.text: "I'm starting to think it wasn't worth it."

264.speaker: Player
264.text: “I gave you a life most woman can only dream of, and this is how you thank me?”

265.speaker: Monica
265.text: "I'll fetch Ciara so you two can get on with your business."

266.speaker: Ciara Walda
266.text: "I did ask her to come to the meeting, as I thought her media traction after the Benfi Festival would make her a valuable spokeswoman. But she told me she was, and I quote, 'barred from politics'."

267.speaker: Narrator
267.text: She shot me a sharp, meaningful look.

272.speaker: Player
272.text: “This is between Monica and myself. Stay out of it.”

273.speaker: Player
273.text: "Monica would only be a liability to your cause.”

274.speaker: Player
274.text: "Be thankful I'm not firing you for approaching her behind my back.”

278.speaker: Ciara Walda
278.text: "First off, Mr. President, I wish to thank you for pushing a decree on establishing gender equality in education. You know this is something I've been trying to accomplish since my appointment as minister. The situation in the public schools was disturbing for me."

279.speaker: Ciara Walda
279.text: "With that said, we still have a long way to go before Sordish women are able to enjoy the same rights and privileges as men."

280.speaker: Ciara Walda
280.text: "These are the measures I believe are most urgently needed."

281.speaker: Monica
281.text: "The two of us talked it over, and these are the measures we believe are most urgently needed."

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: I let my eyes wander down the list.

285.speaker: Player

286.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Mothers"] == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

287.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Workplace"] == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

288.speaker: Player
288.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Education"] == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

304.speaker: Ciara Walda
304.text: "I shouldn't have to tell you how crucial this is. It is utterly unbelievable that, in this day and age, Sordish men are legally allowed to beat their wives."

305.speaker: Narrator
305.text: Ciara looked at me closely, as if she were scrutinizing my reaction. How much had Monica told her?

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "What families do in their own homes is none of our concern."

314.speaker: Monica
314.text: "I'm happy we're on the same page."

315.speaker: Ciara Walda
315.text: "I'm happy we're on the same page."

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: Monica and Ciara both looked disgusted.

318.speaker: Ciara Walda
318.text: "With all due respect, Mr. President, it is. By staying lenient on this we are essentially telling Sordish women that the state doesn't care about them."

319.speaker: Ciara Walda
319.text: "As incidences are especially high within Bludish communities, I would also advocate for setting up a special domestic violence task force in collaboration with Bludish women's rights organizations."

320.speaker: Monica
320.text: "Are you sure that's something we ought to focus on? The Bluds are... different. They have their own rules."

322.speaker: Ciara Walda
322.text: "Monica, I'm surprised at you! We can't let women suffer under the patriarchy, no matter their ethnicity."

323.speaker: Player
323.text: "Interfering in Bludish matters has landed us in enough trouble already."

327.speaker: Player
327.text: "The Bluds have their own ways of settling these issues."

328.speaker: Player
328.text: "We should lift up all Sordish women, Bluds included."

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "The Bluds must conform to Sordish law."

330.speaker: Player
330.text: "I'm still not sure criminalizing domestic violence is a good idea. For the Bluds or anyone else."

334.speaker: Ciara Walda
334.text: "We can discuss the particulars once the law has passed."

335.speaker: Ciara Walda
335.text: "I assure you it is. But I'll give you some time to think about it."

338.speaker: Ciara Walda
338.text: "It simply isn't fair that women in the workforce are punished for having children."

342.speaker: Monica
342.text: "Remember what I told you about Janice? My friend who basically got fired for becoming pregnant? That would never happen to a man."

343.speaker: Ciara Walda
343.text: "Paid maternity leave and state-subsidized daycare centers could be key to keeping more mothers employed."

344.speaker: Player
344.text: "I don't want to reward women for choosing work over raising their children."

345.speaker: Player
345.text: "It's true -- having children never hindered my career prospects. It shouldn't hinder a woman either."

350.speaker: Player
350.text: "Monica, you always said you never regretted giving up a career to raise Franc and Deana."

353.speaker: Ciara Walda
353.text: "What about women who have to work to provide for their children? This could lead to healthier families and a healthier economy."

361.speaker: Ciara Walda
361.text: "I'm happy you agree. In theory, at least."

367.speaker: Ciara Walda
367.text: "Right now, Sordland has one of the continent's largest pay gaps between men and women. We need legislation ensuring that a woman doing the same job as a man is paid the same wage."

368.speaker: Monica
368.text: "We would also introduce quotas to get more women into positions of power -- in the Assembly, for instance, or on the boards of corporations."

372.speaker: Ciara Walda
372.text: "Eventually. Narrowing the pay gap is a far more pressing issue, as it would bring financial independence to countless lower-income women."

373.speaker: Monica
373.text: "Ciara, we never talked about this. But I always thought that with more women in power, higher status for all women would naturally follow."

374.speaker: Ciara Walda
374.text: "Women are starving because they don't make a living wage. That's a damn sight more important than your friend Janice being passed over for a promotion."

375.speaker: Ciara Walda
375.text: "A quota for women in positions of power -- on the boards of large corporations, for instance, or even within the Assembly -- would also be advisable."

376.speaker: Player
376.text: "Quotas are a terrible idea. People should be hired on merit, not simply because of their sex."

377.speaker: Player
377.text: "I don't see a problem with quotas, but tackling the pay gap is much more urgent."

378.speaker: Player
378.text: "Quotas seem far easier to implement than equal pay laws. We should start there."

388.speaker: Narrator
388.text: Monica and Ciara looked at me strangely.

392.speaker: Monica
392.text: "Men are hired on the basis of their sex all the time. Just not consciously."

394.speaker: Ciara Walda
394.text: "Men are hired on the basis of their sex all the time. Just not consciously."

395.speaker: Ciara Walda
395.text: "There are more than enough qualified women to fill any position you can think of. It's up to us to give them the opportunity."

399.speaker: Ciara Walda
399.text: "You know how much this means to me. And you've witnessed the dangers firsthand."

400.speaker: Ciara Walda
400.text: "The way girls are shut out of a real education unless their parents have the means to get them out of the public school system -- so many bright minds are being lost."

404.speaker: Monica
404.text: "I wouldn't entirely demean the old system, Ciara. Deana still loves her handicrafts classes."

405.speaker: Ciara Walda
405.text: "I'm not saying we'll take those away. Maybe boys should learn handicrafts too."

408.speaker: Player
408.text: "We can't force schools what to teach to whom."

409.speaker: Player
409.text: "Yes, we've had this conversation. I'm entirely on your side."

411.speaker: Ciara Walda
411.text: "I'm not saying we'll take those away. Maybe boys should learn handicrafts too."

412.speaker: Player
412.text: "We've had this conversation, Ciara. I'm entirely on your side."

413.speaker: Player
413.text: "My voters won't want to see their sons in an apron."

418.speaker: Ciara Walda
418.text: "We can if not doing so puts us on the wrong side of history. Have you forgotten what we decided about evolution?"

419.speaker: Ciara Walda
419.text: "We can if not doing so puts us on the wrong side of history. I still believe you made a mistake with your creationism decision."

420.speaker: Ciara Walda
420.text: "Good. Then we see eye to eye on the matter."

421.speaker: Ciara Walda
421.text: "But maybe they'll want to see their daughters become the next Artvin Einstavn."

425.speaker: Ciara Walda
425.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Violence"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Mothers"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Workplace"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Education"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

428.speaker: Ciara Walda
428.text: "Especially those who aren't keen on pantsuits."

429.speaker: Monica
429.text: "And convince the public the changes will be beneficial."

433.speaker: Player
433.text: “It's going to be damn hard getting your laws past the Assembly."

434.speaker: Player
434.text: "What do you need a commission for? I'll run your laws past the Assembly."

436.speaker: Ciara Walda
436.text: "Nia would kill me for saying this, but... this is one case where using your decree powers would be fully justified."

437.speaker: Player
437.text: "What exactly is going on between you and Mrs. Morgna, anyway?"

441.speaker: Player
441.text: "Look who's suddenly off her moral high horse."

442.speaker: Player
442.text: "You're right. The Assembly would only pass a weak version of these laws, if at all."

443.speaker: Ciara Walda
443.text: "I know. But even a watered-down version would be better than nothing."

444.speaker: Ciara Walda
444.text: "If it's for the greater good, I have no problem bypassing the Assembly."

445.speaker: Ciara Walda
445.text: "Even if that's successful, you'll still need the commission to ensure the laws are successfully implemented."

449.speaker: Monica
449.text: "And convince the public the changes will be beneficial."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "I've already given women equal access to education. I want to see how that decision shakes out before making any new laws."

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "Sorry, but the answer is no. You can try and run your laws by the Assembly, but they'll get no support from me."
454.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Decree_Stronger"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Decree_Stronger"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

457.speaker: Monica
457.text: "That's all the excitement you can muster? You did it! We did it!"

458.speaker: Narrator
458.text: Monica hugged Ciara. She smiled uncomfortably.

460.speaker: Ciara Walda
460.text: "You're making a mistake by not pushing this through right away. But I'm happy for your support."

464.speaker: Ciara Walda
464.text: "We still have a long way to go. I'll start gathering names for the commission tonight."
464.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Decree_Stronger"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_WomensRights_ThroughAssembly"] == true) == false)

467.speaker: Narrator
467.text: She and Monica headed towards the door. Monica paused before leaving.

475.speaker: Monica
475.text: "Whatever our differences, I'm glad you were able to set them aside and act for the good of Sordish women."

477.speaker: Narrator
477.text: She headed towards the door, then paused and turned back to me.

478.speaker: Ciara Walda
478.text: "I wish your wife could be here right now to celebrate your decision. We both know how much this means to her."

479.speaker: Narrator
479.text: She looked at me one last time before walking out.

480.speaker: Narrator
480.text: I could hear Monica and Ciara talking excitedly to each other as the door closed behind them.

482.speaker: Ciara Walda
482.text: "We've waited long enough, Mr. President. If you aren't re-elected, this opportunity will be lost."

483.speaker: Ciara Walda
483.text: "I suggest you think long and hard about how you're going to explain yourself to your wife. We both know how much this means to her."

484.speaker: Narrator
484.text: She looked at me one last time before leaving the office.

485.speaker: Narrator
485.text: I took a long sip from the bottle of whiskey in my office desk drawer, then picked up the phone and called Monica.

486.speaker: Narrator
486.text: I looked out my window over the city of Holsord. It was a clear day outside.

488.speaker: Monica
488.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Violence"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Mothers"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Workplace"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Education"] == true

489.speaker: Monica
489.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Violence"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Mothers"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Workplace"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_WomensRights_Listened_Education"] == true) == false

506.speaker: Ciara Walda
506.text: "We still have a long way to go before Sordish women are able to enjoy the same rights and privileges as men."

524.speaker: Narrator
524.text: Ciara let out a lengthy exhale. Her face had started to turn red from holding her breath for so long.

525.speaker: Narrator
525.text: As she made eye contact with me, her professional side took hold. She swiftly straightened her posture and put on the icy mask of an experienced politician.

529.speaker: Ciara Walda
529.text: "It's not over yet, Monica. The true battle is in the Assembly. We'll celebrate once that's over with."

530.speaker: Ciara Walda
530.text: "I'll start gathering names for the commission tonight."

534.speaker: Monica
534.text: "I hope this is still as important to you as it used to be. And I trust you to do the right thing."

535.speaker: Monica
535.text: "You never did listen to me about the importance of woman's rights. Maybe you'll take your own minister more seriously."

536.speaker: Narrator
536.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_DenyEverything"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Monica_Opinion"] < -5) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn08_ExtendEmergency_Extend"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Democratic"] < -10)

537.speaker: Monica
537.text: "Anton, I think you'll agree that I've put up with quite a lot over the course of your presidency."

538.speaker: Monica
538.text: "And that man would want a better future for his daughter and her daughters. Just like you told me you did all those years ago."

539.speaker: Monica
539.text: "But despite it all, I look at you and I still see the idealistic, driven man I married."

546.speaker: Narrator
546.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_DenyEverything"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Monica_Opinion"] < -5)

547.speaker: Monica
547.text: "Anton, I think you'll agree that I've put up with quite a lot over the course of our marriage."

551.speaker: Monica
551.text: "But some part of me still sees you as the idealistic, driven man I married."

552.speaker: Narrator
552.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrSelfResigned"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrForcedResign"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_PetrTrialled"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn08_SecondScandal_DenyEverything"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Welfare_FailedEducationReform"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Welfare_EvolutionNotMandatory"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn08_A_WomensRights_MonicaInConversation"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Monica_Opinion"] < -5) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn08_ExtendEmergency_Extend"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Democratic"] < -10) == false)

553.speaker: Monica
553.text: "Anton, I'm not completely naive. I know what we're proposing would have its downsides."

557.speaker: Monica
557.text: "But every time I look at our daughter, I think about how I'd do anything to grant her a better future."

558.speaker: Monica
558.text: “I know you would too. Even if you might not admit it."

559.speaker: Monica
559.text: "I know you would too. Just like you told me all those years ago."

560.speaker: Narrator
560.text: Ciara was looking studiously at a scratch on my desk. She blinked and turned back to us.
